 Judgment
This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, seeking compensation of Rs.27,00,000/- from the respondents, for the grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident. 
2. The brief facts of the case are as follows:
On 17-03-2023 at about 9.45 p.m., the petitioner was riding the motorcycle bearing Reg. No. TN-70-AH-5617 with wearing helmet along with the pillion rider, slowly,
cautiously, by observing all the traffic rules and norms on NH-44 Bommasandra-Chandapura service road and when they reached opposite to Sipan Auto LPG, the driver of the Bolero Pick-Up vehicle bearing Reg. No. KA-01-AL-1236 came in a high speed, rash and negligent manner and dashed to the motorcycle of the petitioner from opposite direction. Due to the impact, the rider and pillion rider fell down on the road. The petitioner sustained grievous injuries and pillion rider died on the way to hospital. Immediately after the accident, the petitioner was shifted to Best Hospital for treatment, thereafter he was shifted to NH Hospital, wherein he took treatment and underwent surgery. Earlier to the accident, the petitioner was working as Safety Engineer at Syngene International Ltd., Biocon Park, Bommasandra Industrial Area and was getting salary of Rs.43,000/- per month. But, due to the above accidental injuries, the petitioner has became permanently disabled and lost his earning capacity. The Hebbagodi Police have registered the case against the driver of the said Bolero Pick-Up vehicle for the offences punishable under Section 279, 337 and 304(A) of I.P.C. The respondent No.1 is the insurer and respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle. Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner. Therefore, it is prayed to allow the petition and award compensation of Rs.27,00,000/- with interest. 
3. On service of notice to the respondents, the respondent No.1 appeared through its counsel and filed the written statement. Whereas, the respondent No.2 remained absent. Hence, the respondent No.2 is placed as ex-parte. 
4. The respondent No.1 in its written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition. It has contended that, the petition is bad for non compliance of provision under Section 134(C) of M.V.
Act. It has denied the age, avocation and income of the petitioner. Further, it has contended that, the alleged accident has taken place due to the sole negligence on the part of the rider of motorcycle and deceased pillion rider, as they were proceeding without helmet and driving licence on a motorcycle Surendhar.R vs Reliance Gen Ins Co Ltd on 5 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/7294064/
2 bearing No. TN- 70-AH-5617 near Bommasandra-Chandapura service road, in a rash and negligent manner, unmindful of the traffic, resulting in the accident. It has denied the issuance of insurance policy in respect of Bolero Pick-Up vehicle bearing No. KA-01-AL-1236. It is further contended that,
the compensation claimed is highly excessive and exaggerated. Further, it sought for permission to contest even on behalf of respondent No.2 as per Section 170 of the Motor Vehicles Act. In view of above denials and contentions, it prayed for dismissal of the petition. 
5. On the basis of rival pleadings of both the sides, the following issues are framed: 
ISSUES 1. Whether the petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries due to the road traffic accident, alleged to have occurred on 17-03-2023, at about 9.45 p.m., due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of Bolero Pick-Up vehicle, bearing Reg. No.
KA-01-AL-1236 ? 
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation ? If so, what is the quantum and from whom ?
3. What order or Award ?
6. In order to prove his case, the petitioner has got himself examined as P.W.1 and got marked 20 documents as Ex.P.1 to 20. Further, he has got examined one more witness namely Dr. S.
Ramachandra as P.W.2 and closed his side. On the other hand, the respondent No.1 has not adduced any evidence on its behalf. Whereas, the respondent No.2 is placed ex-parte. 
7. I have heard the arguments of both the sides and perused the entire material placed on record. 
8. My findings on the above issues are as under:
Issue No.1: Affirmative Issue No.2: Partly Affirmative Issue No.3: As per the final order, for the following:
REASONS 9. Issue No.1: It is specific case of the petitioner that, on 17-03-2023 at about 9.45 p.m., the petitioner was riding the motorcycle bearing Reg. No. TN-70-AH-5617 along with the pillion rider,

Due to the impact, the rider and pillion were fell down on the road, the petitioner sustained grievous injuries and pillion died on the way to hospital. Due to the above accidental injuries, the petitioner has became permanently disabled and lost his earning capacity.

3 10. In order to prove his case, the petitioner has got examined himself as P.W.1 by filing examination-in-chief affidavit and got marked total 20 documents as Ex.P.1 to 20. Out of the said documents, Ex.P.1 is true copy of F.I.R., Ex.P.2 is true copy of first information statement, Ex.P.3 is true copy of Spot Mahazar, Ex.P.4 is Motor Vehicle Accident Report, Ex.P.5 is true copy of wound certificate, Ex.P.6 is true copy of charge-sheet, Ex.P.7 is spot sketch, Ex.P.8 is the discharge summary, Ex.P.9 are the medical bills (9 in nos.), Ex.P.10 and Ex.P.11 are notarised copies of Aadhar cards, Ex.P.12 is 65(B) certificate, Ex.P.13 is copy of appointment letter, Ex.P.14 are pay slips (6 in nos.), Ex.P.15 is bank statement, Ex.P.16 is cashless authorization letter, Ex.P.17 is outpatient slip with clinical note, Ex.P18 is X-ray film, Ex.P.19 is CT Scan report with CD and Ex.P.20 are CT scan films ( 3 in nos). 
11. On meticulously going through the police documents marked as Ex.P.1 to 7, prima-facia it reveals that, on 17-03- 2023 at about 9.45 p.m., the petitioner was riding the motorcycle bearing No.
TN-70-AH-5617 along with the pillion rider, on NH-44 Bommasandra-Chandapura service road and when they were opposite to Sipan Auto LPG, the driver of the offending Bolero Pick-Up vehicle bearing No.KA-01-AL-1236 came in a high speed, rash and negligent manner and dashed to the motorcycle from opposite direction and due to the said impact, the rider and pillion rider were fell down on the road, sustained grievous injuries and pillion rider died on the way to hospital. The investigation officer in his final report has clearly stated that, on the alleged date, time and place of accident, due to rash and negligent driving of the Bolero Pick-Up vehicle bearing Reg. No.
KA-01-AL-1236 the said accident has taken place and the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries on vital parts of his body. Further, the Ex.P.3 spot mahazer also clearly speaks that, the petitioner was proceeding on NH-44 Bommasandra-Chandapura service road and the driver of the Bolero Pick-Up vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-01-AL-1236 dashed him from opposite direction. 
12. The petitioner, who has been examined as P.W.1, has reiterated the entire averments made in the petition. The said facts have remained undisputed by the owner of offending vehicle/respondent No.2, as he did not choose to appear and contest the case of petitioner. Whereas, though the respondent No.1 has specifically denied the said facts in its written statement and in the cross-examination of P.W.1., it has not produced any rebuttal evidence to disprove the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner. Further, the petitioner/P.W.1 has unequivocally denied the suggestion made by the learned counsel for respondent No.1 that, the alleged accident has not occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Bolero Pick-Up vehicle bearing No.KA-01-AL-1236. Further, he has clearly denied the suggestion that, the said accident has occurred due to his own negligence. Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.1 has cross- examined P.W.1 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from his mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of her evidence. 
13. Further, on meticulously going through the Ex.P.5 wound certificate, Ex.P.8 discharge summary,
Ex.P.17 outpatient slip with clinical note, Ex.P.18 x-ray film, Ex.P19 CT scan report with CD and Ex.P20 CT scan films, it clearly reveals that, the petitioner has suffered grievous injuries in a road traffic accident and he has suffered right leg both bone fracture, right hip posterior dislocated with femur head fracture, abrasion over right cheek, punctured wound over left knee, abrasion over right knee, contusion over left lower abdomen and traumatic brain injury. Further, the P.W.2, who is the Surendhar.R vs Reliance Gen Ins Co Ltd on 5 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/7294064/
4 doctor who has examined and treated the petitioner, has clearly deposed in his evidence that, on 18- 03-2023, the petitioner was brought to Mazumdhar Shaw Medical Center at Bengaluru, with the history of road traffic accident and on clinical examination he found that, the petitioner had right leg both bone fracture, right hip posterior dislocated with femur head fracture, abrasion over right cheek, punctured wound over left knee, abrasion over right knee, contusion over left lower abdomen and traumatic brain injury and for the said injuries the petitioner has underwent surgery i.e. right tibia closed reduction internal fixation with IMIL (intra medullary interlocking) nailing and right femur head fracture fragment excision. Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.1 has cross-examined P.W.2 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from his mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence. On the other hand, the respondent No.1 has not led any evidence to substantiate the contentions taken in its written statement. In such circumstances and in the light of above observations, it can be safely held that, the respondent has failed to rebut the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner regarding the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Bolero Pick-Up vehicle bearing No. KA-01-AL-1236 and there is nothing on record to disbelieve the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner.
14. Further, as per the Motor Vehicle Accident Report, which is marked as Ex.P.4, the accident was not caused due to any mechanical defects in the vehicle involved in the accident. When the accident was not due to the any mechanical defects in the offending vehicle, then it can be presumed that, the said accident had occurred due to negligence of the rider of offending vehicle. Further, the investigation officer has clearly stated in the final report, marked as Ex.P.6, that, the alleged accident has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle bearing Reg. No.
KA-01-AL-1236. There is absolutely no rebuttal evidence placed on record by the respondents and even nothing is elicited in the cross-examination of P.W.1 to show that, there is no fault or negligence on the part of rider of offending motorcycle. In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report filed by the investigation officer and other police records,
regarding the negligence of the driver of offending vehicle, place, date and time of accident,
involvement of the offending vehicle and injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident. 
15. Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011)
SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof in a criminal case are not required." 
16. The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Bimla Devi and others V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others , reported in (2009) 13 SCC 513, has clearly held that, " in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims, the claimants are merely required to establish their case on touch stone of preponderance of probability and the standard of proof on beyond reasonable doubt could not be applied." 
17. Therefore, in the light of observations made in the above cited decisions and for the above stated reasons, this Court is of the considered opinion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, he has sustained grievous injuries in a motor vehicle accident, occurred on 17-03-2023 at about 9.45 Surendhar.R vs Reliance Gen Ins Co Ltd on 5 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/7294064/
5 p.m., due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of Bolero Pick-Up vehicle bearing No.
KA-01-AL-1236. Hence, I answer Issue No.1 in Affirmative. 
18. Issue No.2: While answering above issue this Court has come to conclusion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, the accident has caused due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of Bolero Pick-Up vehicle bearing No. KA-01-AL-1236 and he has sustained right leg both bone fracture, right hip posterior dislocated with femur head fracture, abrasion over right cheek,
punctured wound over left knee, abrasion over right knee, contusion over left lower abdomen and traumatic brain injury and for the said injuries he has underwent surgeries. Therefore, this Court is of the further opinion that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under various heads. The damages are to be assessed under two heads i.e. pecuniary damages, such as medical treatment,
attendants, transport, actual loss of earning, future loss of earning etc., and non pecuniary damages,
such as mental and physical shock, loss of amenities, loss of expectation of life, loss of prospects of marriage etc., The petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
i) Towards loss of future income: In order to determine the compensation towards loss of future income, the age, monthly income and disability of the petitioner are to be determined. To prove his age, the petitioner has produced the copy of his driving licence, which is marked as Ex.P.10. As per Ex.P.10, the date of birth of the petitioner is 19-11-1991. The accident has taken place on 17-03-2023 at about 9.45 P.M.
Therefore, the age of the petitioner as on the date of accident is 31 years. Further, the P.W.2, who is the doctor who has examined and treated the petitioner has clearly deposed in his examination-in-chief affidavit that, on clinical examination he found that, the petitioner has suffered traumatic brain injury- diffuse axonal injury, right leg both bone fracture and right hip part dislocated with femur head fracture and for the said injuries the petitioner has underwent surgery i.e. closed reduction and internal fixation with IMIL nailing and right femur head fracture fragment excision.
Further he has deposed that, on clinical and radiological examination of injuries suffered by the petitioner he found that, the petitioner has 68.5% physical disability of right lower limb and for the whole body he has 34.25% physical disability. The oral evidence of P.W.2 is fully corroborated with documentary evidence. The Ex.P.5 wound certificate, Ex.P.8 discharge summary, Ex.P.17 outpatient slip with clinical note, Ex.P.18 X-ray film, Ex.P.19 CT scan report with CD and Ex.P.20 CT scan films clearly speaks that, the petitioner has suffered right leg both bone fracture, right hip posterior dislocated with femur head fracture, abrasion over right cheek, punctured wound over left knee, abrasion over right knee, contusion over left lower abdomen and traumatic brain injury and for the said injuries the petitioner has underwent surgery i.e. right tibia closed reduction internal fixation with IMIL (intra medullary interlocking) nailing and right femur head fracture fragment excision. Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.1 has cross-examined P.W.2 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from his mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence. Further, he has clearly denied the suggestions made to him that, the Ex.P.17 to 20 documents are not related to the petitioner, there is no disability to the petitioner and he has exaggerated the percentage of disability to the petitioner. 
Surendhar.R vs Reliance Gen Ins Co Ltd on 5 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/7294064/
6 But, it is pertinent to note that, the P.W.2 has deposed in his evidence that, the accident has occurred on 17-03-2023 and he has assessed the disability to the petitioner on 27-11- 2023, which is after lapse of eight months from the date of injuries caused to the petitioner. Further he has stated that, the petitioner requires one more surgery for removal of the implants. This clearly goes to show that, the disability has been assessed before the completion of full treatment. As per the gazette notification issued by the Ministry of Social Justice of Government of India, the disability should be assessed after completion of treatment. If the disability had been assessed after future surgery,
perhaps there would have been reduction in the percentage of the disability. Further, it is pertinent to note that, the P.W.2 has clearly deposed in his evidence that, there is union of fractures of tibia of right leg of the petitioner and posterior dislocation of head of right femur (hip joint) shows correction. Therefore, considering the age of the petitioner, injuries sustained, duration of treatment and oral and documentary evidence on record, this Court is of the opinion that, considering the disability of 20% to the whole body of the petitioner would be justified. Hence, in the instant case the physical disability of 20% to the whole body of the petitioner is considered. 
a) The petitioner has deposed in his evidence that, before accident he was working as Safety Engineer at Syngene International Ltd., Biocon Park, Bommasandra Industrial Area and was getting salary of Rs.43,000/- per month. Further, he has deposed that, due to grievous injuries suffered in the said accident he is unable to do his work. The respondent No.1 has specifically denied the same. 
In such circumstances, the burden was on the petitioner to prove his avocation and income. To substantiate the same he has produced copy of appointment letter, pay slips (6 in nos.) and bank statement as per Ex.P.13 to Ex.P.15. From these documents it is clear that the petitioner was working as Associate Executive- Production at Syngene International Limited and drawing salary of Rs.43,000/- per month. 
b) The petitioner has clearly stated in his cross- examination that, his monthly salary is around Rs.43,000/- and now he is drawing salary of Rs.45,000/- per month. Further, he has admitted that,
he has received the salary for the period in which he remained absent for his works. He has applied for the medical leave for the said period and the company has granted medical leave along with salary to him. Now he is working in the same company in the same cadre. This clearly goes to show that, the petitioner is continued in the same job and he is doing same work as he was doing before the date of accident and the disability suffered by him is not affecting his work. Therefore, in such circumstances, the question of awarding compensation for loss of future income due to permanent disability suffered by him does not arise at all. For the disability suffered by him, the petitioner may get compensation under the head loss of amenities and discomfort, but not under the head loss of future income due to disability. Hence, this Court is of the opinion that, the petitioner is not entitled for compensation under this particular head. 
ii) Medical expenses: The petitioner has deposed that, he has incurred expenses of Rs.4,00,000/-
towards medical, conveyance, food & nourishment, attendant charges and other incidental charge. 
Further he has deposed that, out of said amount the medical bill was Rs.3,75,679/-. Out of it the Medi Assist India Pvt. Ltd., through the New India Assurance Company Ltd., has paid Rs.3,16,197/-
only and the balance amount of Rs.59,482/- has been paid by the petitioner. In order to prove the same, he has produced 9 medical bills, as per Ex.P.9. All the bills have been examined carefully and Surendhar.R vs Reliance Gen Ins Co Ltd on 5 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/7294064/
7 found that, the petitioner has spent an amount of Rs.59,482/- towards medical expenses. There is absolutely no evidence on record to show that, the said medical expenses have been reimbursed to the petitioner by his employer/ company. Therefore, this Court is of the opinion that, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.59,482/- under the head of medical expenses. 
iii) Pain and sufferings: In the present case the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries i.e., right leg both bone fracture, right hip posterior dislocated with femur head fracture, abrasion over right cheek, punctured wound over left knee, abrasion over right knee, contusion over left lower abdomen and traumatic brain injury. As per Ex.P.8 discharge summary, the petitioner has taken treatment as inpatient for 08 days from 18-03-2023 to 25-03-2023, in NH Mazumdar Shaw Medical Center,
Bengaluru. He has also underwent surgery i.e., right tibia closed reduction internal fixation with IMIL (intra medullary interlocking) nailing and right femur head fracture fragment excision. 
Further as per P.W.2, the said injuries have caused physical disability to the petitioner. In such circumstances, certainly the petitioner would have suffered pain and sufferings. Therefore, taking into considering the injuries sustained and disability to the petitioner, this Court is of the opinion that, compensation amount of Rs.40,000/- is to be awarded to the petitioner towards pain and sufferings. 
iv) Attendant charges: As per Ex.P.8 discharge summary, the petitioner has taken treatment as inpatient for 08 days from 18-03-2023 to 25-03-2023, in NH Mazumdar Shaw Medical Center,
Bengaluru. He might have spent considerable amount towards attendant charges during that period. 
Therefore, compensation of Rs.1000 x 8 = Rs.8,000/- is awarded towards the attendant charges. 
v) Food and nourishment: As the petitioner has taken treatment as inpatient for 08 days from 18-03-2023 to 25-03-2023, in NH Mazumdar Shaw Medical Center, Bengaluru, he might have spent considerable amount for food and nourishment during that period. Therefore, compensation of Rs.
800 x 8 = Rs.6,400/- is awarded towards food and nourishment charges. 
vi) Conveyance expenses: The petitioner is the resident of T. T. Edayar, Viluppuram T., Edayar,
Tamil Nadu, the accident has taken place at Bommasandra-Chandapura service road and he has taken treatment at NH Mazumdar Shaw Medical Center, Bengaluru. Taking into consideration the distance in between all the above three places, compensation of Rs.4,000/- is awarded towards conveyance. 
vii) Loss of income during treatment period: The petitioner has taken treatment for 8 days as inpatient at NH Mazumdar Shaw Medical Center, Bengaluru, for the grievous injuries sustained by him. The petitioner admitted during his cross-examination that, he has received the salary for the period in which he remained absent for his works. He has applied for the medical leave for the said period and the company granted medical leave with salary to him. Hence, granting compensation for loss of income during the treatment period does not arise in the instant case. Therefore, no compensation is awarded in this particular head. 
viii) Loss of amenities: It is evident from the documents placed on record that, as on the date of accident the age of the petitioner was 31 years and unfortunately he has suffered fracture of weight Surendhar. R vs Reliance Gen Ins Co Ltd on 5 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/7294064/
8 bearing bones. The evidence shows that, he has suffered permanent disability to the extent of 20%
to the whole body. Therefore, awarding compensation of Rs.40,000/- towards loss of amenities would be just and reasonable. 
ix) Future medical expenses: The P.W.2 has clearly deposed in his evidence that, the petitioner needs to undergo one more surgery for removal of implants. But, the petitioner has clearly admitted in his cross-examination that, the medical insurance provided by the company will be applicable for future treatments also. In such circumstances, the question of awarding future medical expenses does not arise at all. Therefore, no compensation is awarded in this particular head. 
19. Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under different heads as follows :
1. Loss of future income Nil 2. Medical expenses 59,482-00 3. Pain and sufferings 40,000-00 4. Attendant charges 8,000-00 5. Food and nourishment 6,400-00 6. Conveyance expenses 4,000-00 7. Loss of income during Nil treatment period 8. Loss of amenities 40,000-00 9. Future medical expenses Nil Total Rs. 1,57,882-00 In all, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,57,882/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization. 
20. Admittedly, as on the date of accident, the respondent No.2 is the owner and respondent No.1 is the insurer of the offending vehicle. Further, the evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Bolero Pick-Up vehicle bearing No.KA-01-AL-1236 the accident has occurred. In such circumstances, the respondent No.2 being the owner of said vehicle is vicariously liable to compensate for the damages caused by the said vehicle. 
The respondent No.1 being the insurer of the vehicle has to indemnify the respondent No.2. 
Therefore, the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner. However, the primary liability is on the respondent No.1 to pay the compensation to the petitioner. Therefore, for the above stated reasons, holding that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,57,882/- from the respondent No.1, I answer Issue No.2 in Partly Affirmative. 
21. ISSUE No.3: In view of the above findings, I proceed to pass the following order:
Surendhar.R vs Reliance Gen Ins Co Ltd on 5 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/7294064/
9 ORDER The petition is partly allowed with costs. 
The petitioner is entitled to compensation of Rs.1,57,882/- (Rupees One lakh fifty seven thousand eight hundred and eighty two only) with interest at the rate of 6%
p.a., from the date of petition till realisation. 
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the above compensation amount. However, the primary liability to pay the compensation amount is fastened on respondent No.1 - Insurance Company and it is directed to pay the compensation amount within two months from the date of this order. 
Out of the compensation amount awarded to petitioner, 30% of the compensation amount with proportionate interest shall be deposited in his name as fixed deposit in any nationalized bank for the period of two years with liberty to draw the accrued interest periodically and the remaining 70% amount with proportionate interest shall be released in favour of the petitioner through e- payment on proper identification and verification. 
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.2,000/-. Draw award accordingly.

(Mohammed Yunus Athani) Member, MACT, Bengaluru.
